eligibility.reason: E1: minimal reproducer plus maintainer diagnosis and correcting PR. E2: rclcpp uses one node guard condition from multiple executor wait sets, while rmw_fastrtps can attach only one condition variable. This is a cross-library usage constraint, not an internal peer-independent failure. E3: PAIR between rclcpp and its RMW provider; the two executors are within the consumer. E4: the newly created subscriber never executes.
eligibility.quote: was that if a node is assigned to multiple executors running asynchronously, it is unable to notify all of them about creating/destroying subscriptions etc..

failed_conditions.quote: was that if a node is assigned to multiple executors running asynchronously, it is unable to notify all of them about creating/destroying subscriptions etc..
failed_conditions.reason: Multiple waiters contend for the single guard-condition attachment. The node notification resource and its wait/trigger APIs are implicated; exclusive_resource_conflict fits this unsupported simultaneous use even though no explicit claim error is raised.

loudness.reason: The documented symptom is a subscription that never executes, not an automatic contract diagnostic; GDB is subsequent manual diagnosis.

detection_stage.quote: Subscriber which is created with dedicated callback group at runtime not working
detection_stage.reason: The issue title explicitly locates creation of the affected subscription at runtime.

resolution.quote: I confirmed that this problem has been addressed by https://github.com/ros2/rmw_fastrtps/pull/619. please feel free to reopen if you still have this issue in rolling.
resolution.reason: The maintainer confirms a fix in rolling, but does not identify both tested revisions. This does not establish the specified rclcpp 16.2.0 / selected rmw_fastrtps resolved revision composition, so recommended is appropriate.

notes: Read both issue timeline pages and the native Fast-DDS WaitSet replacement diff. The private attachment is overwritten and notify_one reaches the attached waiter. The unexecuted subscription is a consequence of the lost notification, not a separately evidenced rate or QoS failure. Switching to Cyclone DDS is supporting diagnosis, not an observed fix of this selected provider pair. No additional independent failed condition found.
